title: Playing a Boston and New York nightclub job with Bechet
summary: He shows a trumpet mute got in Boston and describes going up to visit his sister and joining Bechet's small nightclub group with George Foster.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The New Trumpet Knows The New Trumpet Knows The New Trumpet Knows
Just like the one you've got on your trumpet knows?
Yeah, I got one that, I got that when I was up in Boston. That's the straight new thing. Oh yeah, you went up to Boston? Yeah. With Bishy. And they got them big cup mules, you know.
Yeah. How did you get that job up in Boston with Bishy?

Well, he sat down and asked me when I come, you know. I had my sister living in Mount Vernon, see. So I was working in insurance then, so I said well, I'll go up there and stay a little while, and see my sister, all at the same time and come back home, you see. I never intended to stay away, you understand, but I remember when I got up there, George, George Foster, you know, he was playing bass. So he said to me, Pete, when we go back to New York, you're going to stay with me? I said yeah. Man, I was thinking about staying in New York and nowhere else. What kind of jobs did you play up there?
You play in one place at the time?
Yeah. That was with Sidney by Cheyenne? Yeah.

That was the bar club. There was nothing to it. You weren't playing nothing. You were playing little head tunes and screeching summertime, you know, on a sopranos sax. There was nothing to it. You get on the stand and play 15 minutes like that and get off, you know? Yeah. There was no dancing or nothing. No dancing? Only piano, trumpets, drums, and sopranos sax.
Yeah, from up in New York called George Trump. George Trump.
